subject: The 18 vtable +98h dispatch sites docs/SCENE_ATTACH_LOCAL_FRAMES.md could not close: what each one pushes as the pose local frame, and whether it can carry a scale, a shear or a zero row. Closes all 18. Establishes that the .scn localframe remains the only AUTHORING source of scale but is no longer the only path, that shipClass+6ECh (00491A30) is orthonormal by construction, and that the capture-point garrison respawn (006F3798) reproduces the scaled world matrix of adopted MLandFort entities - the kind carrying 7,075 of the 7,621 scaled localframe statements in this installation.

answer: All 18 open dispatch sites are closed. Eleven push a literal identity (007F48BA, 00484C7D, 00487F16, 0048C819, 00498A61, 0049BD9D, 007A5EB3, 007AB672, 0089AB8E, 00A32433, 009362FE), two are verbatim 16-dword REP MOVSD forwarders of their own matrix parameter (004EA6FB, 004EA80B), one pushes an orthonormal frame built from model geometry (00491A30), one propagates an existing pose local basis unchanged (004B21B3), two propagate a scale an earlier producer put there (006AF842 savegame restore, 006F3798 garrison respawn), and one builds its own basis that is orthogonal but unit only when its heading pair is normalised (0082197D). The .scn localframe is therefore still the only AUTHORING source of scale, but not the only path: three sites carry an existing scale into a new pose local and none multiplies a fresh one in. 00491A30 indexes shipClass+6ECh, a std::vector<Matrix44> with a 40h stride filled only by BSP_ShipClass_BindModelData_Provisional's 'idle' marker loop (00831430-008316FD), whose basis goes through 0085DC80 at 008316E0 and is pushed at 008316ED with NO re-multiply by a scale - unlike the .scn parser at 0046D1BF-0046D222 - so it is a pure rotation always. 006F3798 pushes record+18h of a 64h-stride array at this+778h; the producer 006F5CC0 copies the adopted entity's WORLD matrix at entity+0CCh verbatim with 004134F0 after forcing 00414DB0, and 006F3660 hands it back as a local frame under the world root with arg1 = 0, which is exactly scale-preserving. The three adopted kinds are 1Bh MLandFort, 45h MAirfield, 46h MShipyard; in this installation LandFort carries 7,075 of the 7,621 scaled localframe statements including all 105 'Heavy AA, Japanese' emplacements at s = 0.7069, while Airfield (254) and Shipyard (241) carry none. The model-node question is left at the boundary: node+0F0h is written by no caller of BSP_Matrix_Multiply4x4 and by none of the six ADD reg,0F0h encodings in .text, all five of which are consumers - so the producer is inside the peer-owned model subsystem and the safe assumption is that a mount node CAN scale independently.

published_rules.why: The packet found a genuine pure rule with no native counterpart: 00B63D50's precondition has no guard in the binary, and the arc's scale error has never been published as a function. mount_frame_scale, mount_frame_is_invertible_by_00b63d50, mount_frame_arc_is_exact and mount_frame_arc_reported_pitch are explicit-input predicates a future host calls before handing a frame to the inverse or the arc.
published_rules.validation: Build-tested (scripts/build.ps1, bsp_core and bsp_game, existing ctest reconstructed_math passed). The formula reproduces both figures docs/SCENE_ATTACH_LOCAL_FRAMES.md derived independently: 45.017 degrees for a true 30 at s = 0.7069 and 35.266 degrees at s = 0.866.
published_rules.new_prediction: For s < 1 there is a critical elevation asin(s) above which sin(true)/s leaves [-1,1] and 00521370's asin is a domain error, not a clamp: 44.98 degrees at s = 0.7069, 9.13 degrees at the shipped minimum s = 0.1586. Arithmetic on the published formula, NOT an observed native failure - bsp_game.exe does not reach 00955630, so checklist rule 6 does not apply.
published_rules.tests_rationale: AGENTS.md defaults to none. The formula's only risk is the direction of the division, and that is pinned by two independently published figures quoted in the doc.
